title: Always On Top: Border detaches and persists on desktop after minimizing with Win + D
author: zperel-2nd-account

status.label: Good Always On Top design candidate
status.detail: The Win+D repro is precise, and current Always On Top border lifecycle code handles ordinary minimize/restore but has no explicit Show Desktop or hidden-window repro coverage.

next_action.label: Approve the border lifecycle design
next_action.reason: The reported shell transition and the current code boundary are concrete enough to queue a fix design, but a local repro is still valuable before implementation.

judgment.rationale: The issue cleanly isolates a reproducible Always On Top border lifecycle failure: Win+D hides the target window, but the border remains visible and detached and does not reattach on restore. Current code handles ordinary minimize start/end but not this exact shell transition.
evidence: The issue gives a deterministic six-step repro using Win+Ctrl+T followed by Win+D.
The border remains visible on the desktop and stays detached after the windows are restored.
Current AlwaysOnTop::HandleWinHookEvent tears down the border for EVENT_SYSTEM_MINIMIZESTART and recreates it for EVENT_SYSTEM_MINIMIZEEND.
Current UI tests cover normal minimize and restore but do not include Show Desktop or taskbar-peek visibility transitions.
judgment.recommended_action: Queue an Always On Top border-lifecycle fix that explicitly handles the Show Desktop / hidden-window transition and add focused Win+D regression coverage.

fix_assessment.rationale: No existing linked PR covers the Win+D detached-border regression, and the current code boundary is narrow enough to propose a focused lifecycle fix.

proposed_fixes.title: Reset and recreate Always On Top borders across Show Desktop transitions
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Always On Top explicitly removes and recreates border objects for minimize start/end, but the Win+D shell path appears to hide or cloak the pinned target without taking the same minimize event path, leaving the old border window alive and detached from the restored target.
plan: Audit the Win+D and taskbar-peek event sequence against AlwaysOnTop::HandleWinHookEvent and refresh logic, then teach the border lifecycle to drop the border when the target is shell-hidden or cloaked.
Recreate or reposition the border only after the target becomes visible and stable again, preserving the pinned state and topmost enforcement.
Add a focused Always On Top UI regression that pins a window, invokes Win+D, restores the desktop, and asserts both border disappearance and reattachment.
verification: Pin a normal window, press Win+D, and confirm the border disappears with the hidden window instead of staying on the desktop.
Press Win+D again or otherwise restore the window and confirm the border reattaches to the live frame and tracks movement.
Retain the existing normal minimize/restore and virtual-desktop border behaviors.

confidence.rationale: The code already shows a narrow lifecycle distinction between minimize handling and generic visibility refresh, but a local Win+D event trace would confirm exactly which shell events must be covered.

issue_context.summary: Win+D hides the pinned window but leaves the Always On Top border rendered on the desktop and detached after restore. The current code and tests suggest a narrow hidden-window lifecycle gap rather than a broad feature defect.
known_information: The reporter is on PowerToys 0.100.2 from GitHub or auto-update.
The issue is specific to Always On Top and uses a deterministic repro with Win+Ctrl+T followed by Win+D.
After restore, moving or resizing the target window does not reattach the border.
There are no comments, attachments, assignees, or linked PRs on the live issue.
inferences: The Show Desktop path likely does not surface as the same minimize transition the code already handles explicitly.
Because the border remains detached until PowerToys restarts, the bug is likely in border-window lifecycle rather than the pin state itself.
issue_context.analysis: The issue is specific enough to queue a design immediately: the shell transition is deterministic, the current code boundary is narrow, and the current UI tests show the missing regression slot.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the full issue body, labels, assignees, and empty live timeline.
Inspected AlwaysOnTop::HandleWinHookEvent and RefreshBorders, which explicitly handle EVENT_SYSTEM_MINIMIZESTART and EVENT_SYSTEM_MINIMIZEEND but not an issue-specific Show Desktop path.
Reviewed the Always On Top UI tests and found coverage for normal minimize/restore but no Win+D or taskbar-peek border visibility scenario.

design.title: Reset and recreate Always On Top borders across Show Desktop transitions

actions.note: Draft only; no upstream code, PR, comment, or issue write is authorized by this artifact.

actions.label: Reproduce Win+D detached border state

prerequisites: Enable Always On Top and use a normal non-elevated application window.
Keep PowerToys running long enough to observe the border before and after Show Desktop.
steps: Pin a normal window with Win+Ctrl+T and confirm the colored border is visible.
Press Win+D to show the desktop and observe whether the border disappears together with the window.
Press Win+D again to restore the windows, then move the restored pinned window.
reproduce.expected_result: The border should hide with the minimized or hidden window and reattach cleanly after restore.

actions.note: Local maintainer reproduction only; no upstream write is performed by this artifact.
